title: Unilateral owner control over dispatcherHook, windowDuration, topUp, pauser, and stakedId creates multiple high-leverage centralization points
description:
The `onlyOwner` admin holds several powerful levers, none of which are time-locked or role-segregated:

1. `setDispatcherHook` — can repoint to an arbitrary `IBalancerPoolerMintDebtHook` contract. Since `_syncBudget` measures `inflow = balanceOf(this) - pre` and credits that to `rewardBudget`, a malicious replacement hook can mint unlimited phUSD to this contract (assuming it has mint rights) and credit it as emissions. Alternatively the owner can zero it to strand dispatcher mint-debt.
2. `setWindowDuration` — can choose any duration in [MIN_WINDOW=1 day, MAX_WINDOW=10 years]. Combined with CS-06, the owner can manipulate the emission rate by 3650x.
3. `topUp` — writes arbitrary `rewardBudget` onto the contract. Owner can also use this to reset `windowEnd` on demand (front-running, etc.).
4. `setPauser` — owner can change the pause authority, including to themselves or to an address they control, bypassing any intent of role segregation.
5. `setStakedId` — only callable when `totalStaked == 0`, but in combination with a pause-and-drain (emergencyWithdraw is the only escape but requires users to act) the owner can force a migration that users did not consent to.

None of these actions are guarded by a timelock or emit a warning period. Users have no 'check-in' window to react before a rate/hook/duration change takes effect on the next block.
impact: Owner-driven emission manipulation, fund redirection via hook replacement, or forced pool reconfiguration.
proof: Standard centralization concern: admin key compromise or rogue-governance action gives direct control over emission schedule and funding source.
recommendation: Put `setDispatcherHook`, `setWindowDuration`, `setStakedId`, and `setPauser` behind a timelock (e.g., 48 hours). For `setWindowDuration` specifically, additionally bound each call to a bounded multiplicative change (e.g. `newDuration <= 2 * currentDuration && newDuration >= currentDuration / 2`) with a cooldown, OR require that the post-change rate not fall below some fraction of the current rate (e.g. `newRate >= currentRate / 2`). This preserves flexibility while removing the one-tx rug path. For `topUp` the window-reset behavior should be opt-in (`topUp(amount, resetWindow)`) rather than automatic. Consider splitting roles: a `SCHEDULER_ROLE` for window/rate changes and a separate `CONFIGURATOR_ROLE` for hook/staked-id changes.
mergeNote: ES-06 merged in: same root cause (owner can dilute or zero active emissions via setWindowDuration mid-stream; no timelock, no cooldown, no per-call magnitude bound). ES-06 quantified the worst case: rate reduction factor = oldWindowRemaining / newWindowDuration; with newDuration = MAX_WINDOW (3650 days) and oldWindowRemaining = 1 day, that's a 99.97% rate reduction in one tx. Floor-division makes it even sharper: if `rewardBudget < newDuration` after the change, the new rate is zero and emissions halt entirely until re-top-up. See also CS-06 for the specific code-level ordering bug in setWindowDuration (accrues under OLD rate without first calling _syncBudget) that compounds this.
